issues.failure_explanation: The maps f and g are T-valued, so tf(x)+(1-t)g(x) mod 1 has no canonical real representatives. Changing a representative by an integer changes the interpolated value, and endpoint agreement on the dense loop set does not establish a uniformly continuous homotopy on all of G.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, replace the linear interpolation with a rigorous construction of a homotopy from equality of all loop degrees, or prove a valid classification theorem for maps C(G,T).
issues.overall_effect: The assertion that equal degree vectors characterize homotopy classes, and the interpretation of the main uniqueness theorem in terms of homotopy classes, are unsupported.
issues.title: Converse homotopy proof uses ill-defined linear interpolation
issues.why_classification: The converse of a central classification theorem is invalid, and the source provides no alternative nontrivial argument; repairing it requires new proof content.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated boundary conditions prescribe only increments and degrees, which are invariant under adding a constant in T. The construction fixes f(v_1^0)=0, so it can prove uniqueness only for a normalized class of maps, not for the theorem as stated.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed energy sums geodesic distances, while the real-valued graph energy sums squared differences. Even when lifted edge differences are small, d_T is not equal to the squared lift difference, so the asserted equality and variational minimizer conclusion are invalid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define \hat\cE_m using squared geodesic distance or squared lift differences where the oscillation is small, and redo the limiting argument.
issues.overall_effect: The variational interpretation that the projected fundamental-domain function minimizes the circle-valued energy functional is unsupported.
issues.title: Circle-valued energy is defined with distance, not squared distance
issues.why_classification: The defect is a local incorrect energy definition; squaring the distance preserves the intended variational framework.
